title: Standard Demo v1 - Internal Dry Run #1 (talk track + console run-through)
summary: Internal dry run of the Standard Demo v1 using the demo tenant. Team walked through the opening narrative, the Hosted API quickstart (streaming), a routing/fallback moment, and the Console dashboards (latency + token cost). Main feedback: transitions between “why Redwood” → “what we’ll show” → “console proof” were unclear; too much time spent on setup screens; need a cleaner handoff line when pivoting to Dedicated/Private. Several contingency notes captured for live demo reliability (dashboard lag, output variance, and what to do if streaming drops).
topics: Opening story: serving economics (latency/cost/reliability) vs model access
Scenario order: 2-min hosted mini-demo vs full standard flow
Console clickpath: Routes → Policies → Fallback + Rollouts
Dashboards: latency p95, 5xx, throttles, token cost breakdown
How to talk about output variance / nondeterminism
When to pivot to Dedicated vs Private (security persona)
questions: Do we say “KV cache” out loud or keep it as “caching” unless asked?
Can we safely claim ‘automatic fallback’ without showing the exact policy rule live?
Where do we park the ‘pricing’ conversation if they push during demo?
action_items: Soojin Lee - Rewrite transition lines between sections (Hosted → reliability/fallback → observability) and add speaker notes for handoffs by 2025-08-16
Renee Sullivan - Create a 2-minute hosted API mini-demo variant (streaming curl + one screenshot) and add to enablement folder by 2025-08-20
Simran Kaur - Lock the canned prompts/expected outputs for Scenario 1 and Scenario 2; add ‘Plan B’ output snippets for variance by 2025-08-19
Markus Klein - Update the console clickpath checklist (exact menu names + where to pause) and include a dashboard-lag contingency by 2025-08-18
Talia Benson - Capture timing targets per section (intro 3 min, hosted 6 min, routing 6 min, dashboards 6 min, wrap 3 min) and post in Confluence by 2025-08-15
next_steps: Schedule Dry Run #2 focused on security persona branch + FAQ handling
Decide final scenario order for Standard Demo v1 (full vs mini first)
Confirm which screenshots are required for deck v1 and which can be optional
transcript:
Fireflies.ai Transcript

Meeting: Standard Demo v1 - Internal Dry Run #1 (talk track + console run-through)
Date: 2025-08-13
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 47 minutes

Attendees
- Stephanie Nguyen (Redwood - Sales)
- Markus Klein (Redwood - Solutions Engineering)
- Soojin Lee (Redwood - Product Marketing)
- Talia Benson (Redwood - Program Mgmt)
- Renee Sullivan (Redwood - Enablement)
- Simran Kaur (Redwood - Demo Scenarios)

---

[00:00] Stephanie Nguyen: Alright, cool. This is dry run one for the standard demo. Goal today is not perfection, it’s like, what feels confusing, what breaks, what’s the awkward parts.

[00:10] Markus Klein: Yep. And we’re using the demo tenant, not my personal sandbox. So if it’s slow, that’s data too.

[00:16] Soojin Lee: And I’m gonna be kind of annoying and stop you on transitions. Like, if I don’t understand why we’re clicking, prospects won’t.

[00:23] Talia Benson: I’ll keep time. I’ll call out if we’re drifting.

[00:28] Renee Sullivan: Also I’m here to translate into enablement assets. So if there’s a repeatable “line” that works, I’m stealing it.

[00:34] Simran Kaur: I have the prompt set open. And I have the canned outputs if we need to paste.

[00:41] Stephanie Nguyen: Great. Okay I’ll do the opening like I’m on a call. Markus you drive when we get into console.

[00:49] Stephanie Nguyen: So, thanks everyone for the time. High level: Redwood’s focus is serving—latency, cost, reliability—across hosted, dedicated, and private. The model landscape changes weekly, but your product SLOs can’t.

[01:07] Soojin Lee: Pause. That line is good. But then you need the “what you’ll see” line. Right now it’s like a thesis but no map.

[01:14] Stephanie Nguyen: Yep. So what we’ll do is: one, make a streaming request so you can see the latency and developer surface area; two, show a failure-mode with fallback routing; and three, show the observability—token cost, errors, latency—so it’s not magic.

[01:30] Talia Benson: 1:30 in.

[01:33] Markus Klein: Cool. I’ll share screen now.

[01:36] Markus Klein: (screen share) You should see the Redwood Console. This is the demo tenant. I’m on Routes.

[01:44] Renee Sullivan: Quick note: can you bump zoom? The left nav is small.

[01:47] Markus Klein: Yep. Sorry. Okay.

[01:52] Markus Klein: Stephanie, do you want to narrate “hosted” now?

[01:56] Stephanie Nguyen: Yeah. So for hosted, the pitch is: you get an API that’s stable, you can pin versions, and you get the knobs without having to become GPU people.

[02:08] Soojin Lee: Careful with “pin versions” unless we show it. Or say “you can pin model versions in the route config” and then we actually click it later.

[02:14] Markus Klein: We can click it. It’s under the route settings.

[02:17] Markus Klein: Okay I’m going to the Quickstart tab. We have the curl.

[02:23] (crosstalk)

[02:24] Markus Klein: This is the streaming chat endpoint. I’ll run it in the embedded terminal.

[02:30] Simran Kaur: Use Prompt A, the “support agent” one. That one is stable-ish.

[02:35] Markus Klein: Copying. Running.

[02:39] Markus Klein: You’ll see tokens stream. (pause) It’s… streaming.

[02:44] Stephanie Nguyen: So right there, that’s a pretty basic thing, but like, a lot of teams get tripped up on “why is it slow sometimes” and “how do I control cost.”

[02:53] Soojin Lee: The “basic thing” downplays it. You could say: “this is what your app integrates with.” Make it feel like day one value.

[03:00] Stephanie Nguyen: Got it. “This is the exact interface your app uses.”

[03:03] Markus Klein: Output looks fine. It’s answering.

[03:07] Talia Benson: 3 minutes.

[03:10] Markus Klein: Now, the part that’s confusing in the narrative is: do we jump to dashboards now, or do we do fallback while we’re in routes?

[03:17] Stephanie Nguyen: I think fallback next, because it’s like reliability, then dashboards as proof.

[03:21] Soojin Lee: Agree, but you need a clean sentence. Like: “Now let’s assume the real world happens.”

[03:26] Renee Sullivan: Yeah, “stuff breaks” line.

[03:29] Markus Klein: Okay. So I’m back on Routes. There’s a route called “standard-demo-chat”. It has a policy.

[03:38] Markus Klein: Here’s Primary model: Redwood-verified Llama something—sorry, the name is long. And fallback is… the smaller variant.

[03:46] Simran Kaur: For the demo we should say: “primary high quality, fallback compatible.” Don’t get stuck on model branding.

[03:52] Markus Klein: Right.

[03:55] Markus Klein: So I’ll toggle the “simulate capacity constrained” flag.

[03:59] Soojin Lee: Wait do we actually have a “simulate” toggle in production? Or is this demo-only?

[04:04] Markus Klein: It’s in the demo tenant only. It’s basically a routing rule override. We should not call it a feature.

[04:10] Stephanie Nguyen: Then we need to phrase it like: “we’re going to force a failure so you can see the behavior.”

[04:15] Markus Klein: Exactly.

[04:17] Markus Klein: Okay. Forcing primary to error. Now I rerun the same request.

[04:24] Markus Klein: Running.

[04:27] Markus Klein: And you’ll see in the response headers, it says “routed-to: fallback.”

[04:32] Simran Kaur: If that header doesn’t show, just scroll to the trace panel. Sometimes the terminal truncates.

[04:37] Markus Klein: Yeah, fair.

[04:39] Markus Klein: It did route. It still streams.

[04:42] Stephanie Nguyen: So this is the “stay online” story. Your app doesn’t go dark because a single model endpoint is having a day.

[04:50] Soojin Lee: That’s good. Add one clause: “and you can control the tradeoff.” Otherwise it sounds like magic.

[04:56] Stephanie Nguyen: Right. “You choose whether fallback is lower cost, or lower latency, or a regional failover.”

[05:04] Talia Benson: 5 minutes.

[05:06] Markus Klein: Now do we go to dashboards? Or do we show the policy rule itself?

[05:10] Soojin Lee: If we show the policy rule, keep it short. People glaze over.

[05:14] Renee Sullivan: I think one screenshot in the deck might be better than live clicks.

[05:18] Markus Klein: Okay, I’ll just open it, point at the “fallback chain,” and leave.

[05:23] Markus Klein: (click) Here. It’s basically: if error rate above X, route to this. There’s also region option.

[05:31] Stephanie Nguyen: And then transition: “We don’t ask you to trust us, we show you what it did.”

[05:37] Soojin Lee: Yes. That’s the missing handoff.

[05:40] Markus Klein: Great. Going to Observability.

[05:43] Markus Klein: Dashboard: Demo Tenant Overview.

[05:47] Markus Klein: You can see p50/p95 latency, tokens per second, and token cost. There’s also 5xx and throttles.

[05:57] Talia Benson: We’re good on time. But don’t camp here.

[06:00] Markus Klein: Okay. The panel “Cost per request” is… loading.

[06:05] Renee Sullivan: That’s the thing that will happen live.

[06:08] Markus Klein: Yeah. Sometimes the query takes a bit. I can say: “these are near-real-time.”

[06:14] Soojin Lee: Don’t say “near-real-time” unless we can define it. Maybe “a couple minutes of ingestion.”

[06:20] Markus Klein: Okay. “A short ingestion delay.”

[06:24] Markus Klein: The latency panel is updating though. p95 is like 780ms.

[06:30] Stephanie Nguyen: And the key is: you can break this down by route and model, right?

[06:34] Markus Klein: Yep. See filter: route = standard-demo-chat. Model = primary vs fallback.

[06:40] Simran Kaur: If the cost panel doesn’t load, go to the saved view “Token Cost Breakdown v1.” It’s lighter.

[06:46] Markus Klein: Good call. I’ll switch to that.

[06:50] Markus Klein: (click) Here. It shows input tokens, output tokens, cache hits—uh, “prefix cache.”

[06:57] Stephanie Nguyen: Say “caching.” If you say “prefix,” it invites rabbit hole.

[07:02] Markus Klein: Got it. “Caching.”

[07:05] Soojin Lee: Also, earlier you said “don’t become GPU people.” That’s cute but it can sound dismissive. Maybe “you don’t have to build and operate your own inference stack.”

[07:14] Stephanie Nguyen: Yep.

[07:16] Talia Benson: 7 minutes.

[07:18] Stephanie Nguyen: Can we pivot to Dedicated in one minute? Like “if you need isolation.”

[07:23] Markus Klein: Sure. I can show the “capacity” page.

[07:27] Soojin Lee: But we should not pretend this tenant is Dedicated. We’re just describing the path.

[07:31] Stephanie Nguyen: Totally. Okay: “Hosted gets you started. Dedicated gets you predictable throughput and isolation.”

[07:38] Markus Klein: There’s a tab “Deployments.” It shows “Hosted” and “Dedicated Pools.” In demo tenant we only show the UI.

[07:46] Renee Sullivan: That might be a deck-only slide. Live clicking into “Dedicated Pools” and seeing “no pools” looks bad.

[07:52] Markus Klein: True. It’s empty.

[07:54] Soojin Lee: Let’s mark that as a change. For live demo, keep Dedicated as narrative + diagram, unless we can seed a fake pool card.

[08:02] Simran Kaur: We can seed a “sample pool” card without real capacity. But that’s product work-ish.

[08:08] Markus Klein: Yeah, not sure we want to fake product.

[08:11] Stephanie Nguyen: I’d rather be honest. Slide + talk track is fine.

[08:16] Talia Benson: If we’re going to do the full thing, we need a hard stop on “deployment modes” at like 2 minutes.

[08:22] Stephanie Nguyen: Okay.

[08:24] Markus Klein: One more thing: error analysis view. I can show the trace for the fallback request. That’s nice.

[08:31] Soojin Lee: Yes. That’s “proof.” Do that.

[08:34] Markus Klein: (click) Request logs. Here’s the request. Open trace.

[08:41] Markus Klein: It shows: policy evaluation, primary attempt failed (forced), then fallback succeeded.

[08:48] Renee Sullivan: That’s good. It’s like a story.

[08:51] Stephanie Nguyen: And if someone asks “how do you know,” we show this.

[08:56] Soojin Lee: Great. Now, let’s talk about what felt weird.

[09:00] Stephanie Nguyen: Yeah, let’s stop the “demo voice” and critique.

[09:04] Soojin Lee: First big thing: we didn’t say upfront what the three proof points are, and we didn’t use signposts like “Now we’ll show reliability.”

[09:12] Stephanie Nguyen: Agree.

[09:14] Markus Klein: Second: the dedicated/private pivot is awkward. If we’re not showing it live, it needs to be a clean branch: “If you have regulated data, we do Private; if you need predictable throughput, Dedicated.”

[09:25] Talia Benson: And timing. We got to dashboards at minute 6-ish. In a real call, we need dashboards earlier or shorter intro.

[09:32] Renee Sullivan: Or we have the 2-minute hosted variant. Like, streaming + one dashboard screenshot. For folks who only give you 10 minutes.

[09:40] Simran Kaur: Also, the output variance. Today it was okay. But we need a line when it says something weird.

[09:46] Stephanie Nguyen: Like “LLMs are probabilistic; we test against prompt sets and watch regressions.”

[09:52] Soojin Lee: Exactly. Also: “we’re not optimizing for one golden prompt, we’re optimizing for predictable serving.”

[10:00] Markus Klein: Another awkward bit: I said “simulate capacity constrained.” That’s internal only. In front of a prospect, I should say “we’re forcing an error.”

[10:10] Talia Benson: Plus the dashboard lag. That cost panel pause was… 10 seconds? It felt like forever.

[10:16] Markus Klein: Yep. Plan B is saved view. Or just say “here’s a screenshot from earlier today” and move.

[10:23] Renee Sullivan: We should standardize that. Like: if panel doesn’t load in 5 seconds, go to saved view. If that fails, show deck screenshot.

[10:32] Soojin Lee: Add that to the runbook.

[10:35] Stephanie Nguyen: What else?

[10:37] Simran Kaur: The prompt selection. We need “known good prompts” labeled and not ad hoc. Also: for tool calling scenario we didn’t run it today.

[10:46] Markus Klein: Tool calling is a longer flow. Might be scenario 3, optional.

[10:51] Soojin Lee: For demo v1, we may not need tool calling if it derails. The differentiator is serving controls + observability.

[11:00] Stephanie Nguyen: Agree. Tool calling is table stakes now.

[11:03] Renee Sullivan: Still, some folks ask. We can keep a backup snippet.

[11:07] Talia Benson: Okay, can we do a quick second run of just the opening + the signposts? Like first two minutes. Soojin wants transitions.

[11:15] Stephanie Nguyen: Sure. Reset. “Thanks for the time…”

[11:19] Stephanie Nguyen: Today I’m going to show three things: first, the developer API experience with streaming responses; second, how Redwood keeps apps online with routing and fallback policies; third, the observability that lets you measure latency and unit cost per route, so you can tune serving economics.

[11:38] Soojin Lee: Much better. Now add: “and we’ll do it in ~12 minutes, then Q&A.” That sets expectations.

[11:45] Stephanie Nguyen: Right. “We’ll do this in about 10 to 12 minutes.”

[11:49] Markus Klein: Great.

[11:51] Talia Benson: Okay. We don’t need to re-run the clicks.

[11:55] Renee Sullivan: One more thing: pricing slide. Are we avoiding numbers entirely? Because AEs keep asking.

[12:01] Stephanie Nguyen: In the live demo, no numbers. We can say “usage-based, plus reserved capacity for dedicated.” If they push, we set a follow-up with their volume.

[12:10] Soojin Lee: And we can reference “ranges” but not quote anything. Marketing wants it safe.

[12:16] Markus Klein: Also, competitor landmines. People will ask “why not Bedrock.” We should have one sentence.

[12:22] Stephanie Nguyen: “Bedrock is great for access; Redwood is optimized for serving controls + consistent economics across environments.”

[12:29] Soojin Lee: Yep, and don’t talk down. Just “different focus.”

[12:33] Talia Benson: We’re at 12 minutes. Let’s move to action items.

[12:37] Renee Sullivan: I captured: mini-demo variant, clickpath checklist, and the transition lines.

[12:43] Simran Kaur: And I’ll lock prompts + expected outputs. Plus Plan B paste.

[12:48] Markus Klein: I’ll update the clickpath and the “if dashboard panel lags” rule.

[12:53] Stephanie Nguyen: And Soojin, you own the narrative edits.

[12:57] Soojin Lee: Yes. I’ll do speaker notes with explicit signposts and handoffs.

[13:03] Talia Benson: Cool. I’ll post timing targets and schedule dry run #2. Probably early next week.

[13:09] Stephanie Nguyen: Awesome. Thanks everyone.

---

(Transcript continues with light scheduling chatter)

[13:14] Renee Sullivan: Tuesday or Wednesday is better for enablement.

[13:18] Markus Klein: Wednesday morning I’m on another customer call.

[13:21] Talia Benson: I’ll send a poll.

[13:24] Stephanie Nguyen: Cool, done.

End of meeting.
